@graph.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon puts gated access at the center
@graph.description: Google will gate Gemini 4 Carbon to cyber defenders first. We separate access claims, benchmark methods, independent results and missing safety documents.

mainEntity.name: Is Gemini 4 Carbon available to everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: No public general-availability date was stated in Google’s 28 October announcement. Google said a subset of cyber defenders would receive access first, then additional trusted partners through Fairwind, followed by developers, businesses and consumers through product surfaces “as soon as possible.” The announcement describes a staged sequence, not a public signup date.

mainEntity.name: Are Google’s cybersecurity benchmark results independently verified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all in the same way. Google says it self-computed the SEC-bench Pro and ExploitGym results. It says CWE-bench comes from the public leaderboard evaluated by Collinear AI. Artificial Analysis reports a separate general capability index score. These sources provide different kinds of evidence and do not establish identical independent reproduction for each benchmark.

mainEntity.name: Does “without guardrails” mean Carbon will ship without safeguards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says its external cybersecurity evaluations were run without guardrails, and separately says it is iterating on guardrails during the staged rollout. Evaluation conditions describe how a test was run; they do not by themselves establish the safeguards in a future product deployment.

mainEntity.name: Does Fairwind’s published MFA requirement apply to Carbon?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Fairwind page checked for this draft describes controls for Gemini 4 Argon, including phishing-resistant MFA, background checks and restrictions on which teams may use the model. The Carbon announcement refers to staged Fairwind access but does not state that every Argon-specific condition already applies to Carbon. Wait for Carbon-specific terms before assuming they are identical.

mainEntity.name: Is the 59 Artificial Analysis score a cybersecurity score?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Artificial Analysis calls it an Intelligence Index v5 score, a broader capability measure. It is separate from SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym and CWE-bench. It provides an external evaluation reference, but it cannot validate or replace the specialized cybersecurity results.
